# biwurth

> A wall-tablet panel for Home Assistant. This website (port 2323 on the tablet) edits what the
> panel shows: pages of tiles on a grid. Everything below is a JSON API on this same address.

## Access

Every /api/* call needs the header `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The key is in the tablet's
Settings (tap the panel's top-left corner five times); ask the user for it. Without it the API
answers 401. Bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`).

Ask the user before anything that changes the panel: saving a layout, page or tile changes, undo,
backup restore, updates, settings, or clearing the log. Reading is always fine.

## Layouts

A layout is `{columns, rows, orientation, theme, background, pages: [{id, name, tiles: [...]}]}`.
A tile is `{id, type, x, y, w, h, props}` on whole grid cells (default grid 12 × 8, stretched
over the whole screen). Prop values are strings. `theme.gap` is the space between cards in dp
(0-32, default 8) and `theme.animations` (default true) makes graphs draw in, values roll and live
dots pulse. A tile's `background: "none"` drops its card so it sits on the panel's background.

A `space` tile (Empty space) keeps its cells empty, down to 1×1: use it for deliberate gaps, or
to reserve room before auto placement. Give it `props.picture` to show a picture there: upload
with PUT /api/picture (body: the raw JPEG, PNG, WebP or SVG bytes) and use the file name it
returns. SVG is drawn as vectors, sharp at any size, so icons and logos work well on 1×1. `fit`:
default shows all of the picture, "cover" fills the tile, "stretch" fills it exactly.
GET /api/picture/<name> returns a picture. Backups include the pictures the layout uses.

- GET /api/schema: grid size, screen size in pixels, themes, backgrounds, and every tile type
  with its props, allowed values, default and minimum size, and which entity domains it takes.
  Read this first.
- GET /api/entities?q=<words>&domain=<domain>: entities to show, each with its state, unit,
  domain, whether it's numeric, and `tiles`: the tile types that suit it, best first.
- GET /api/layout: the saved layout.
- POST /api/layout/check (body: a layout): checks without saving. Returns the layout as it would
  be saved and `report.issues`: `{code, message, page, tile, entity}` with codes overlap,
  too_small, no_entity, entity_missing, not_numeric, wrong_domain, unknown_field, not_checked,
  no_stream, background_missing.
- POST /api/screenshot (body: a draft layout, or `{"layout": …, "page": n}`): a PNG of that page
  as the tablet draws it, made off-screen; nothing is saved or shown. GET /api/screenshot?page=n
  for the saved layout. Query: scale=0.1-1 (0.5 is plenty to judge a layout), format=jpeg,
  settle=<ms>. Takes a few seconds; cameras show a snapshot.
- PUT /api/layout (body: a layout): saves it; the panel switches to it. Returns the report.
- GET /api/layout/history, POST /api/layout/undo: every save keeps the layout it replaced (20 of
  them); undo puts back the last one.

Leave out a tile's x and y and it goes in the first free spot (left to right, top to bottom) after
the tiles that have one, in list order. Leave out w and h for its type's default size. So a page
can be written as an ordered list of tiles with sizes, and the positions come back filled in.

## Themes and page templates

The layout's look is `theme`: `preset` (a built-in colour preset: dark, graphite, nord, forest,
light, or an installed theme's id), `accent`, `font`, `textScale`, `tileOpacity`, `gap`,
`animations`, `cards` (cards behind tiles by default; a tile's `background` "card"/"none"
overrides) and `tiles`, how tiles are drawn:

    radius, padding, borderWidth (dp)    borderColor "#rrggbb" ("" = theme's muted)
    shadow (dp, 0 = none)                valueWeight light|regular|bold (big numbers)
    titleWeight regular|medium|bold      titleColor muted|text      titleDivider true|false
    toggleStyle fill (lights up) | switch (a switch, card unchanged)
    clockWeight thin|light|regular       graphGrid, graphFill true|false   graphLineWidth (dp)
    graphColors ["#rrggbb", …] (line colours; empty = accent, then built-in ones)
    tileLayout stacked (name over a big number) | compact (icon beside name and value)
    icons none | badge (tinted circle, Mushroom) | bubble (plain circle, Bubble Card)
    buttonShape card | pill (value and toggle tiles fully rounded)
    toggleStyle also icon (only the icon lights up when on)
    listDividers (lines between calendar events)
    calendarColors (a tile of several calendars marks each event in its calendar's graphColors colour)

Value and toggle tiles take `props.icon`: one of bed, bolt, bulb, calendar, coffee, computer, drop, fan, gauge, home, moon, plug, power, snowflake, sun, thermometer, tv, or "none"; by
default the compact layout picks one from the entity (temperature: thermometer, power: bolt, …).

Calendar tiles show today's events with the date in the accent colour and later ones muted; text
grows with the tile's width.

Built-in themes: aurora (dark, glowing gradient, line icons) and ant-design (Ant Design's light
look: white bordered cards, title lines, switches, grid lines, AntV chart colours).

A theme package is a zip:

    theme.json          {"id": "lowercase-id", "name", "description", "base": a built-in preset,
                         "colors": {background, card, text, muted, accent, onAccent},
                         "font", "textScale", "tileOpacity", "gap", "animations", "cards",
                         "tiles": {…as above}, "background": {…, "image": "backgrounds/x.jpg"}}
    pictures/…          SVG, PNG, JPEG or WebP for Empty space tiles
    backgrounds/…       background pictures
    templates/<n>.json  page templates: {"name", "description", "tiles": [...]}; a tile's
                        "picture": "pictures/x.svg" uses the theme's own picture

- GET /api/themes: installed themes with their colours, settings, pictures and templates.
- POST /api/themes (body: the zip): installs or replaces one. Its pictures become
  "theme-<id>-<file>" for tiles' `picture`.
- POST /api/themes/<id>/apply: puts its look (and background) on the layout and saves.
- GET /api/themes/<id>.zip: its package. GET /api/themes/current.zip?id=…&name=…: the current
  look, pictures and pages (as templates) as a new theme, a good start for making one.
- DELETE /api/themes/<id> (not the built-in ones).
- GET /api/templates: page templates, the app's (builtin/…) and themes' (<theme>/…).
  GET /api/templates/<id> for one. POST /api/templates/page {"template": id, "name"?} adds a page
  from it; its entities are usually empty, so fill them in (PATCH the tiles) and check.

Small changes without resending the whole layout (each saves, and undo goes back; <page> is a
page id or its number from 0):

- POST /api/layout/pages {name, tiles?}: add a page.
- PATCH /api/layout/pages/<page> {name}, DELETE /api/layout/pages/<page>.
- POST /api/layout/pages/<page>/tiles {type, w?, h?, x?, y?, props}: add a tile.
- PATCH /api/layout/pages/<page>/tiles/<tile> {x?, y?, w?, h?, type?, props?}: props merge into
  the tile's; "" or null removes one.
- DELETE /api/layout/pages/<page>/tiles/<tile>.

## Designing a layout

1. GET /api/schema and GET /api/entities?q=… for what's available.
2. Write the page; let auto placement position tiles unless the arrangement matters.
3. POST /api/layout/check and fix every issue.
4. POST /api/screenshot?scale=0.5 with the draft and look at it: text that's cut off or tiny,
   empty areas, tiles too small for their content. Repeat 2-4.
5. Show the user the screenshot, and save (PUT /api/layout) when they agree.

## Panel

- GET /api/status: screen state, page shown, Home Assistant and MQTT connection, and `memory`:
  the panel's own use (appMb, PSS), what the tablet has left (deviceAvailableMb), `warning` when
  it's close to full, and `suggestedMaxLive` live camera streams for its RAM; `cameras`: camera
  tiles on the panel, the live limit (`maxLive`, set with PUT /api/cameras) and how many play.
- GET /state, POST /wake, POST /sleep: the screen.
- GET /api/config: layout, MQTT, cameras and screen settings in one.
- GET /api/logs: the last 500 log lines (plain text); GET /api/logs/all for all of them.
- GET /api/cameras: go2rtc stream names; GET /api/cameras/status: how each camera tile is doing.
- GET /api/update: installed and latest version.
- POST /api/benchmark?seconds=5-60&mode=idle|full|swipe&warm=0|1: measures drawing on the tablet
  (wakes the screen): idle leaves it, full redraws everything every frame, swipe goes through the
  pages; warm adds a speck of drawing every frame. Returns fps, frameMs {p50, p90, p99, max},
  overBudgetPercent (frames over the display's frame time), cpuPercentOfCore. Use it to compare a
  layout or theme change. The panel must be on screen.
- PUT /api/screen {"showFps": true}: an FPS counter on the panel.
- GET /api/presence: wake on motion. `inventory` (cameras, sensors, microphone), `plan` (detectors,
  thresholds, notes on why), `live` (watching, change %, room brightness, motion now, last motion
  and what saw it). PUT /api/presence {enabled, keepAwake, sensitivity -2..2}.
  POST /api/presence/calibrate?step=still|moving&seconds=15: calibration where the panel hangs:
  "still" with nobody in view, then "moving" with someone walking in front; each makes the plan
  again. Needs the panel on screen and the "Backlight off" sleep mode. Home Assistant (MQTT) gets
  a Motion and a Room brightness sensor.
